partnershipPlan: Two owner representatives review the consult-room notice and the tablet-giving handout before cycle 1; the head nurse and one veterinary surgeon per clinic join the monthly feedback review.
socialListening: No social media listening; the clinics' own review pages and complaint log from the last year are read for comments on injections, tablets and antibiotics.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I cannot get a tablet into her without being scratched; the injection was the only thing that worked for us.
items.implication: Offer nurse tablet-giving appointments and keep an injection option with a recorded reason.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I did not mind leaving without antibiotics once the vet explained the diarrhoea should settle and told me when to come back.
items.implication: Put an explanation and a recheck plan in the consult-room guide.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: At ten minutes a consult, a pop-up that needs a paragraph will just get owner request typed into it.
items.implication: Use a short pick-list of reasons with optional free text and review the reasons each cycle.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If we are the ones showing owners how to give tablets, we need an appointment slot, not five minutes at the desk.
items.implication: Schedule nurse tablet-giving appointments from cycle 3.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I can pull the weekly report in a quarter of an hour, but only if the drug list is fixed before we start.
items.implication: Fix the HPCIA product list in the operational definition before the baseline.

summary: Five composite voices shaping tablet support, owner explanation, the prompt design, nursing time and the fixed measure.
